statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-9076 ("Out-of-Bounds Read in CMS Password-Based Decryption", Low): when an application decrypts attacker-supplied CMS data with password-based decryption (CMS_decrypt() or CMS_decrypt_set1_password(), or openssl cms -decrypt -pwri_password), a stream-mode key-encryption cipher chosen by the attacker can make kek_unwrap_key() read a few bytes past a heap buffer, which can crash the application. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.6 are affected and 3.5.7 is fixed (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt); the fix on the 3.5 branch is https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/715349a1d7c6db970e6815dafb90915f07307f98, which rejects KEK ciphers with a block size below 4 bytes. The advisory states that the OpenSSL FIPS modules are not affected. The openssl-fips packages built from this source, in the DHI security repository, hold the OpenSSL FIPS provider module (fips.so) and its configuration files; the version string in each build's fips.so, read on x86_64 and aarch64, is the OpenSSL release that the package version names (3.5.5 through 3.5.9). None of those fips.so files contains CMS code (the names of the CMS and password-recipient (PWRI) functions are not found in any of them, while AES-256-GCM is found in each, and the same search finds them in the OpenSSL libcrypto), so those packages are not affected even where the range reads them as affected. The DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl packages are built from the upstream OpenSSL source release that their version names, with Alpine's packaging patches, so 3.5.7-r0 is the first published build that contains the fix. The debug symbols in openssl-dbg (x86_64) confirm this: ossl_cms_RecipientInfo_pwri_crypt, into which kek_unwrap_key is inlined, is 1734 bytes in 3.5.6-r0 and 3.5.6-r1 and grows to 1802 bytes in 3.5.7-r0 and 3.5.7-r1. Every earlier published build (3.5.4-r0 through 3.5.6-r1, including 3.5.5_git20260330-r1) is affected.

CVE-2026-9076 ("Out-of-Bounds Read in CMS Password-Based Decryption", Low): when an application decrypts attacker-supplied CMS data with password-based decryption (CMS_decrypt() or CMS_decrypt_set1_password(), or openssl cms -decrypt -pwri_password), a stream-mode key-encryption cipher chosen by the attacker can make kek_unwrap_key() read a few bytes past a heap buffer, which can crash the application. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.6 are affected and 3.5.7 is fixed (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt); the fix on the 3.5 branch is https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/715349a1d7c6db970e6815dafb90915f07307f98. The advisory states that the OpenSSL FIPS modules are not affected. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 (DSA-6335-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-9076). The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages built from that source onward, in both the DHI Debian repository and the FIPS builds in the DHI security repository, carry the fix: the changelog shipped in libssl3t64 of the first of those builds and of both FIPS builds of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 lists CVE-2026-9076 under 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, and on amd64 the debug symbols show ossl_cms_RecipientInfo_pwri_crypt, into which kek_unwrap_key is inlined, growing from 2316 bytes in the last 3.5.6-1~deb13u1 builds (main and FIPS) to 2374 bytes from 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 on. The fixed version is the lowest published build of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2. Every published build of earlier Debian sources (3.5.5-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, including their FIPS builds) is affected. The openssl-provider-fips packages built from this source, in the DHI security repository, contain only the FIPS provider module (fips.so) and its documentation. The version string in each build's fips.so, read on amd64 and arm64, is OpenSSL 3.5.5, 3.5.6 or 3.5.7 (matching the Debian source version) in the openssl-provider-fips packages of the non-FIPS builds, and OpenSSL 3.1.2 in those of the FIPS builds; the libssl3t64 packages ship no fips.so. None of those fips.so files contains CMS code (the names of the CMS and password-recipient (PWRI) functions are not found in any of them, while AES-256-GCM is found in each, and the same search finds those names in libcrypto), so the provider packages are not affected even where the range reads them as affected.
